16 A box slides down a rough ramp.
The change in the gravitational potential energy of the box is 16 J as it moves between positions
X and Y. The box has 24 J of kinetic energy at X and 35 J of kinetic energy at Y.
box
ramp
X
Y
How much work is done against the frictional force?
A
5 J
B
19 J
C
27 J
D
43 J

hints: Notice the box already has $24\text{ J}$ of kinetic energy at X and $35\text{ J}$ at Y, so find the actual gain in kinetic energy first.
Connect the $16\text{ J}$ loss of gravitational potential energy to that kinetic gain: on a rough ramp some potential energy becomes kinetic energy and the rest is used working against friction.
Calculate work against friction as lost gravitational potential energy minus gained kinetic energy, both in $\text{J}$, and compare with the options.
walkthrough: Identify the given energies: gravitational potential energy decreases by $16\text{ J}$ from X to Y, kinetic energy at X is $24\text{ J}$ and at Y is $35\text{ J}$.
State the energy principle for a rough slope: loss in gravitational potential energy = gain in kinetic energy + work done against friction.
Find the gain in kinetic energy: $35 - 24 = 11\text{ J}$.
Rearrange for friction work: work against friction = potential loss - kinetic gain.
Substitute with units: $16\text{ J} - 11\text{ J} = 5\text{ J}$, which checks as energy in $\text{J}$.

A.explanation: The $16\text{ J}$ lost from gravitational potential exceeds the $11\text{ J}$ gained in kinetic energy by $5\text{ J}$, which is the work done against friction.

B.explanation: Adding the $16\text{ J}$ potential change to the $35-24=11\text{ J}$ kinetic change is incorrect because friction removes energy rather than adding it.

C.explanation: Adding $24\text{ J}$ and $35\text{ J}$ and subtracting $16\text{ J}$ mixes total energies incorrectly and does not give energy lost between X and Y.

D.explanation: Adding $24\text{ J}$, $35\text{ J}$ and $16\text{ J}$ is incorrect because only the change in kinetic energy, not the sum, is linked to work done.
